newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Nike plant in Vietnam hit by brief strike.
newsitem.headline: Nike plant in Vietnam hit by brief strike.

text.p: About 800 workers went on strike over pay and labour conditions last week at a plant in Vietnam that makes shoes for Nike Inc, a Labour Department official said on Monday.

Friday's three-hour stoppage at South Korea's Sam Yan Co. factory near Ho Chi Minh City followed several weeks of controversy over alleged worker abuse at Asian factories contracted by the American sportswear giant.
The Labour Department official, who declined to be named, said the workers downed tools at noon on Friday because a new collective contract offered them a pay rise of just five percent.
Newspaper reports said that under the 1997/98 contract, the workers would receive 470,000 dong ($40.32) a month.
The employees went back to work when it was explained to them that Ministry of Labour regulations require employers to raise wages by a total of 10 percent over two years, not one.

The official said the strikers also demanded that labour contracts be presented to the workforce at least two days before they were required to sign them, and complained that supervisors sometimes shouted at factory workers.
Nike's office in Hong Kong declined to comment immediately on the dispute.

Meanwhile, an Indonesian plant that makes Nike shoes closed for the weekend following protests over wages by thousands of workers on Friday. Local news reports said some of the workers ransacked an office and damaged cars.

Last month, Vietnam Labour Watch accused three South Korean and Two Taiwanese factories producing Nike shoes in Vietnam of abusing their workers. The group said some workers were limited to one trip to the lavatory and two drinks of water per shift, and that verbal abuse, sexual harassment and corporal punishment were common.
Nike has said it cannot confirm the group's findings, but has stressed it welcomes and works with independent observers to monitor, train and improve working conditions overseas.

Also, a supervisor at a Taiwanese plant is to stand trial soon for alleged abuse of employees. The woman is accused of making 56 workers jog twice around the two-kilometre (1.2-mile) factory perimeter for failing to wear regulation workshoes.
